A welcome from the Head Teacher, Miss Matthews
Welcome to our Willen Primary School website. We hope that this website will give you an idea of life here at Willen Primary School and will encourage you to join us. We are a values led school and we work tirelessly to create a learning-centered, happy, secure and caring environment. This is a school where each individual is valued and respected.
We prepare children for life in a modern world by providing opportunities where children can thrive and grow. We pride ourselves on offering a stimulating, challenging and diverse curriculum where children of all abilities are able to make fantastic progress. We believe that Willen is ‘A Place Where Everyone Flourishes’ so we have adopted this as our school motto. As a primary school, we keep English and maths as core features of our teaching, however, we place a great emphasis on developing the ‘whole’ child. To do this we provide a wide range of experiences for our children. We have a dedicated and active WSA (our parents’ association). With their support, we have extended our facilities for outdoor learning and redeveloped the school libraries. The children are continually making excellent use of the new resources.
We look forward to seeing you soon.
Miss Carrie Matthews, Executive Head Teacher

pageCache.text:
Art
Curriculum Intent- Art
At Willen, individual creativity, exploration and expression are at the heart of our art curriculum. We aim to inspire children to become artists, designers and architects. Our art curriculum enables all children to communicate what they see, feel and think through the formal elements of line, shape, form, tone, texture, pattern, colour and composition through different materials and techniques. From the beginning in the EYFS, the children are taught to develop their ability to respond to the work of the ‘greats’[1] and their own work in an individual way. They will become art detectives, describing, discussing, analysing, interpreting and making personal judgements about a variety of works of art. We will focus on 7 media types - dry media (including drawing), painting, printing, collage, textiles, 3D (including sculpture) and digital art. Each skill becomes one of 7 art units to be taught across a 2 year cycle to ensure breadth, depth and clear progression of skills and knowledge. Each unit title has the name of an artist to study and be inspired by. Underpinning the whole curriculum (from Y1-Y6) is the story of each child’s artistic journey through their sketchbooks. There are also strong curriculum links which will be capitalised on - DT through structure and architects and textiles and Computing through digital media and animation. Art skills will be used to creatively express linked learning and home learning outcomes in subjects such as history and R.E.
[1]The greats refers to those significant artists from our heritage plus artists who are living, female and represent our culturally diverse community including local artists to Milton Keynes and those from the LGBT community.

RE
Curriculum Intent- RE
At Willen we aim for our Religious Education curriculum to engage, challenge and encourage children, helping them to gain knowledge and skills to be able to explore different religious beliefs, values and traditions. We aim to equip them with an understanding of the religious traditions, beliefs and practices that are followed in our multicultural society. We want our Religious Education to contribute to enabling pupils to combat prejudice, preparing them for adult life, employment and life-long learning.
We follow the Milton Keynes agreed syllabus which aims to grow ‘religious literacy’ so that pupils can be confident in expressing their own religious understanding and respectfully learning from others of different religious backgrounds. The curriculum builds on the skills and knowledge that the children acquire. We aim to enrich the curriculum through visits from local faith groups, through assembly reflection and looking at places of worship in our local area.

Modern Foreign Languages
Curriculum Intent- MFL
At Willen Primary School we believe that:
Implementation of MFL
Regular MFL lessons are provided in all KS2 year groups through engaging, relevant topics and famous people. Vocabulary and language skills are developed every lesson through a logical sequence building on previous knowledge.
The curriculum, focusing mainly on French to enable pupils to make substantial progress in one language, gives pupils the ability and confidence to express their ideas and thoughts in another language and to understand and respond to its speakers, both in speech and in writing. The same teacher teaches French across KS2 (PPA cover).
As the class teacher does not teach MFL, LanguageNut planning is used in all year groups to provide consistency, structure and build on previous skills.
Differentiation is provided by the different assignable tasks, adaptable interactive games and adult support in the classroom.
The French teacher records attainment in line with the whole school assessment policy using the scores provided as a guideline.

pageCache.text:
Design Technology
Curriculum Intent- Design Technology
At Willen Primary we believe that:
Children at Willen engage in at least 3 Design and Technology units each academic year. These units have been carefully selected and mapped out as part of a whole school curriculum. Each unit builds on skills and knowledge they will have gained previously. Where it makes logical sense the unit links to other subjects covered by that year group at the same time.
Units of work typically are taught as a block with sessions taught consecutively for between 4 and 8 days. Sometimes a unit may be spread out with one lesson being taught each week over a term. Design Technology is usually taught by the class teacher.
Each year group will complete a food technology unit and typically a structures or mechanics unit. In KS2 there are also units with a computer aided design focus. In the Early Years DT is taught mostly through continuous provision and play.
During their time at Willen children will engage in a range of design activities multiple times with a spiral approach to building on previous learning. Units will include a mixture of market research, product testing, designing, making, prototyping, adapting, marketing, and evaluating. However not all units will involve all stages of the design, make, evaluate, review process and not all units will culminate in a finished product.
Feedback on progress can be made during or after lessons, with the children afforded time to make improvements to their work. Often, children will evaluate their own work or take part in peer assessment. This is reflected in our whole school assessment policy.
Children are generally taught as a whole class, for the research, design and evaluation parts of a unit but may, for practical or safety reasons, divide into groups for the construction, cooking or engineering of a design.
Lessons will frequently allow students to apply skills and knowledge from other subjects especially English, Maths, Science and Computing however we do not require onerous recording of ideas, designs or evaluations. At Willen we very much want the focus to be on the design and make skills rather than ability to write them down. Teachers are given license to be creative in how they get their pupils to demonstrate their understanding and progress.
Each unit starts with a unit overview that is shared with the children. This acts as an intent statement and helps children understand what they will be learning and how. The structure of the planning of the unit is then the responsibility of individual teachers.
Individual lessons and the whole units will vary greatly in terms of content and structure. Over the course of the year children will focus on different elements of the subject as outlined below. Each unit but not each session will include teacher led activities, discussions and active learning. There will be time given for experimentation, creativity and skills practice.
Differentiation will mainly be through the level of adult support each child receives. Generally, children will not be given different activities to complete. This may also be seen through the use of enabling and extending techniques.
The Design Technology curriculum is carefully designed to cover six key principles. Pupils and teachers should be aware of these and how they impact the designs and products that are produced at Willen. They are:
User - Pupils should have a clear idea of who they are designing and making products for, considering their needs, wants, values, interests and preferences. The intended users could be themselves or others, an imaginary or story based character, a client, a consumer or a specific target group.
Purpose - Pupils should be able to clearly communicate the purpose of the products they are designing and making. Each product they create should be designed to perform one or more defined tasks. Pupils’ products should be evaluated through use.
Functionality - Pupils should design and make products that work/function effectively in order to fulfil users needs, wants and purposes. It is NOT enough to design and make products that are purely aesthetic.
Design Decisions - Pupils need opportunities to make their own design decisions. They need to have chances to show their creative, technical and practical expertise, and use learning from other subjects. The decisions they make need to be more than just how it looks and should include how it works, materials used, tasks it will perform and the user but not necessarily all in the same project.
Innovation - When designing and making, pupils need some scope to be original with their thinking. They should not be taught how to make something and then replicate it but instead be taught skills that may be useful to complete a more open ended task.
Authenticity - Pupils should design and make products that are meaningful and relevant to themselves and others. These may not always be products that can be entirely produced or taken home but they should know that in theory they could be and if they were made they would be valued and worthwhile.
The Design Technology curriculum taught is both knowledge and skills based. There is a clear outline for the progress of skills to be taught in each year group and each unit has specific knowledge that must be disseminated for pupils to be successful. During most units pupils will also learned about a notable designer, engineer, chef or producer that should help to inspire ideas and spark ambition.

Geography
Curriculum Intent- Geography
At Willen Primary we believe that:
Implementation of Geography
At Willen Primary, our Geography curriculum follows the programmes of study set out in the National Curriculum. Pupils study three Geography units each academic year. Children in all year groups develop their place and locational knowledge, understanding of physical and human geography and geographical and fieldwork skills. Each unit has been carefully selected and mapped out as part of a whole school curriculum to ensure progression of skills and knowledge across and within year groups. The structure, planning and lesson content is then the responsibility of individual teachers.
Where it makes logical sense, units may be linked to other subjects covered by that year group at the same time to promote cross-curricular learning. Strong links between Geography and English are specially planned for in the form of cross-curricular writes.
Typically, one Geography unit is taught in the Autumn term, one in the Spring term and one in the Summer term. Units usually run for a half term, comprising around 6 lessons taught weekly by the class teacher. Geography alternates with History each half term.
There is a strong focus on outdoor learning and children make use of the school grounds and surrounding area to develop awareness of their locality.
Feedback on progress can be made during or after lessons and attainment is recorded with Target Tracker in line with the whole school assessment policy.
Differentiation will mainly be through the level of support and scaffolding each child receives. Generally, children will not be given different activities to complete. This may also be seen through the use of enabling and extending techniques.

pageCache.pageTitle: After School Clubs and Wrap Around Care – Willen Primary School
pageCache.text:
After School Clubs and Wrap Around Care
Extra-Curricular Clubs
Willen staff offer a variety of 'after school' activities for children at no or minimal costs. A half termly 'menu' of activities is sent to families at the start of each new term.
Please email office@willenprimary.org for the most up-to-date menu.
Wrap Around Care
For more than 20 years, Premier Education has been delivering high-quality provision to primary schools nationwide, offering physical education, holiday camps, and a wide range of extra-curricular activities across both sporting and non-sporting subjects.
In 2016, we expanded our services to include wraparound care, bringing together our expertise in active, engaging provision with a convenient and seamless experience for parents. Our commitment to creating healthy, active, and enriching environments has made us the trusted choice for a growing number of schools.
From May 2023, Premier Education is proud to be partnering with Willen Primary School to deliver exceptional wraparound care.
Our Wraparound Provision
Running every day the school is open, end of school day until 6:00 pm, our wraparound care offers a safe, fun, and nurturing environment that both children and parents can trust.
What Premier Education Wraparound Offers:
Engaging Activities – From gymnastics to gardening, children can enjoy a wide variety of fun, active, and stimulating experiences.
Nutritious Meals & Snacks – A balanced menu designed to meet school food standards.
Easy Online Booking – A straightforward system with instant confirmation, helping parents manage sessions effortlessly.
Responsive Support – Our friendly team is available by phone or email, ensuring quick and helpful responses to any queries.
Flexible Scheduling – Book up to 1:00 PM on the same day, perfect for last-minute changes.
Stress-Free Refunds – With our ‘Flexi Bookings’ option, parents can claim a no-questions-asked refund for any missed session.
We’re thrilled to be supporting families at Willen Primary School and look forward to welcoming your child to Premier Education Wraparound Care!
Life at Our Wraparound Care
Our wraparound care offers a true home-from-home environment, where children can relax, recharge, and feel at ease after a busy school day. Whether they’d like some quiet time or prefer to dive into exciting activities, there’s always something to enjoy in our warm and nurturing environment.
Every session is packed with fun and creativity. Children can lose themselves in imaginative play, build amazing structures with Lego, K’NEX, and building blocks, explore their artistic side at our creative stations, while our end-of-week movie night—complete with popcorn—offers the perfect opportunity to unwind with friends.
Alongside free play, we provide an enriching programme of adult-led activities designed to spark curiosity and broaden horizons. From edible crafts and construction challenges to team games and global themes, our sessions inspire children to learn about the wider world in engaging, stimulating ways. They might create traditional art from different cultures, engineer international landmarks, or take part in group challenges inspired by customs from around the globe.
More than just a wraparound club, we’re a community. Whether your child joins us every day or just now and then, they’ll always feel at home here.
Timings & Prices for Wraparound Care
We provide flexible wraparound care designed to fit your family’s routine, offering a safe, engaging, and fun space for your child before and after school. Sessions run every day the school is open, with different pick-up times to suit your schedule.
Session Options & Pricing:
All sessions include a wide variety of activities, from creative play to team games, plus a healthy snack in line with school food standards. Children staying until 6:00 pm will also enjoy a light tea, served between 5:00 pm and 5:15 pm.
How to Book Our Wraparound Care
Booking your child’s place at Premier Education Wraparound Care is quick and easy. Simply visit Premier Education – Willen to get started.
New to Our Services?
If you’re booking with us for the first time, you will need to create an account. As part of the registration process, we will collect some important details—such as medical and dietary information—so we can provide the best care and support for your child.
Booking Your Sessions
Once your account is created, simply log in, choose your sessions, and confirm your booking in just a few clicks. You’ll receive an instant email confirmation, making it easy to keep track of your child’s schedule.
Important Information
To maintain safe staff-to-child ratios, all sessions run on a first-come, first-served basis, with bookings accepted until 1:00 pm on the same day. We encourage booking early to guarantee your child’s place.
If you have any questions or need help with bookings, our friendly support team is here to assist. We look forward to welcoming your child to our wraparound care!

Holiday Camps – Fun & Engaging Childcare When School’s Out!
At Premier Education, we understand that school holidays can be a juggling act for busy parents—that’s why we provide exciting, high-quality childcare when schools are closed. Our holiday camps, running at venues across Milton Keynes, offer a safe and vibrant environment where children can stay active, make friends, and take part in a wide variety of activities.
As the UK’s leading provider of sport and physical activity, we deliver expert coaching and fun, engaging games at every camp. But the experience doesn’t stop at sport—children also enjoy arts & crafts, outdoor adventures, team challenges, and themed enrichment activities that spark creativity and curiosity.
With flexible booking options and a programme designed to suit different ages and interests, our holiday camps give parents peace of mind while offering children days filled with fun, learning, and new experiences.

Our Curriculum
Curriculum Intent
We want every child to leave Willen Primary School fully prepared for the next stage of their life. We want children to believe in themselves and their potential to make a real difference in the world. Willen Primary School is: ‘A Place Where Everyone Flourishes’
At Willen Primary school we have a varied and exciting curriculum in which we aim to develop the whole child. This curriculum enables us to help your child to gain a secure understanding of the world in which they live in and develop their own sense of self. We want learning to be fun and enjoyable so that the children reach their potential and have the opportunity to flourish! We want to build experiences and memories that will stay with the children as they progress both through the school and through their lives.
A running thread throughout our bespoke Curriculum is that of 'people'. This does not mean 'famous people' - but the potential of all human beings to make a positive difference; from inventors to sports personalities, from acts of altruism to activism!
During the mornings (typically) the children have core lessons of Maths and English where they are taught in an engaging and diverse way. The children have the opportunity to learn in a range of different ways including real life maths, and drawing upon 'WOW' events and moments in their English learning. In addition to this we also develop multiplication skills to ensure quick recall of multiplication and division facts and develop their understanding of Grammar, Punctuation and Spelling as well as having engaging and stimulating whole class guided reading sessions.
We teach the foundation subjects on a weekly basis . Within these lessons the children have the opportunity to make connections in their learning and work across a range of subjects and skills. All of our curriculum lessons have a focus on skills which the children will build upon as they move across the school. We endeavour to make cross curricular links such as writing instructions in English lessons of how to make soup which was taught in a DT lesson; promoting connections and depth of understanding.
In addition to this at WPS, we believe that education is not all about the 3 R’s. Alongside the wonderful experiences that the children’s families plan for them, we have developed 'Enrichement Planners' for each year group across the school. This is our commitment to enriching the life experiences of the children whilst they are in our care and developing the cultural capital of the children.
If you would like to find out more about our curriculum, Mrs Nickson would be happy to help you. Contact her via office@willenprimary.org

Maths
At Willen Primary School, our maths curriculum is designed with the belief that every child can achieve their full potential. We operate on the principle that success in mathematics is not predetermined; our teaching embodies a growth mindset, encouraging students to believe in their ability to improve. Our approach focuses on depth of understanding before expanding the breadth of knowledge. This ensures that all pupils progress together, with lessons accessible to every learner.
We maintain high expectations for all students, instilling in them confidence and a love for mathematics. This is a collective effort, valued by staff, pupils, parents, and carers alike, fostering a community of confident and successful mathematicians.
We are proud that our Maths Lead is now a recognised Primary Mastery Specialist and Local Leader of Mathematics Education (LLME), who works with the Enigma Hub and the National Centre for Excellence in the Teaching of Mathematics (NCETM) to bring best practices to our school. We align our planning with NCETM Curriculum Prioritisation and Oak Academy materials to ensure coherent and high-quality learning experiences. From Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) to Year 5, we employ the Mastering Number program to enhance fluency and recall of number facts.
Implementation of Maths Mastery
Our teaching embraces the Maths Mastery approach, utilizing resources from NCETM and Oak Academy. Feedback is provided during and after lessons, with dedicated time for students to refine their work. Whole-class teaching is the standard, supplemented with adult support when necessary.
We provide regular opportunities for students to engage in reasoning, problem-solving, and fluency exercises. To deepen understanding, our lessons incorporate concrete, pictorial, and abstract representations. Lessons are structured in small, conceptual steps to strengthen connections and ensure comprehensive understanding.
We incorporate spaced practice and retrieval activities to help students retain knowledge over time. Additional support is promptly provided to ensure all students can access subsequent lessons. For students who quickly grasp concepts, challenge tasks are available to explore greater depth rather than accelerating through the curriculum.
Dialogue is central to our teaching, fostering discussions between teachers and pupils, as well as among pupils themselves. We allow flexible topic durations, ensuring sucient depth of learning. Adaptive teaching is primarily facilitated through adult support and the use of enabling and extending tasks. Assessment is recorded on Sonar and supplemented by informal tools from NCETM.
Our curriculum builds robust mathematical foundations and instills confidence in our students. It aids in long-term knowledge retention and supports the development of fluency, reasoning, and problem-solving skills.
How Parents Can Help
Parents play a crucial role in reinforcing their child's mathematical learning. Here are some ways you can help:
Practice Number Facts: Incorporate games and quick quizzes to make learning fun. Encourage Reasoning: Ask your child to explain their thinking and reasoning behind solutions.
Support Homework: Engage with your child's homework and discuss mathematical concepts in everyday situations.
Celebrate Effort and Progress: Emphasise the importance of effort and progress, not just correct answers.
For more information, feel free to contact us via email at oce@willenprimary.org, addressed to Mrs. Prescott, our Maths Lead. Visit our website for additional resources and updates.

Science
Curriculum Intent- Science
At Willen, we aim to give children a strong understanding of the world around them whilst acquiring the skills and knowledge to help them think scientifically. We hope to develop and nurture our children’s curiosity by not only following the National Curriculum, but by following their own questions and interests to develop a love, passion and appreciation for science. Children will be encouraged to understand how science can be used to explain what is occurring, predict how things will behave and analyse causes.
We ensure that the Working Scientifically skills are built-on and developed throughout the children’s time at Willen Primary School so that they can apply their knowledge of science when using equipment, conducting experiments, building arguments and explaining concepts confidently and continue to ask questions about their surroundings. We like to make use of the school grounds to support and enrich our learning, as well as bring in scientists for school visits who the children can aspire to be like. We also place a strong emphasis on learning about inspirational scientists who have played a major role in areas linked to the topics we have learnt about. This year, Willen Primary School is working towards a Primary Science Quality Mark and will seek to build on all of the aspects written above.
